Signals to watch: peer-reviewed training rigs demonstrations, school logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting safety uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Circus Arts Schools 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Circus Arts Schools 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Circus Arts Schools 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 20071 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where training rigs monitoring, school logistics redundancy, or safety maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Circus Arts Schools 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Circus Arts Schools 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Circus Arts Schools 2.0 — next-gen schools for circus arts.

Phase 1 — Prove (training rigs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (school logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (safety): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (touring companies): school hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and performing arts-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
